name: Český Krumlov
tagline: Bohemia's fairy-tale town, a medieval castle and pastel old town wrapped almost entirely by a horseshoe bend in the Vltava River.
highlight: Looking down from the castle tower at dusk, the old town's red rooftops curling around the river exactly as they have for centuries.
shortDescription: Bohemia's fairy-tale town, a UNESCO-listed medieval old town wrapped in a horseshoe bend of the Vltava River beneath a dramatic hilltop castle.
metaDescription: A Český Krumlov travel guide: the castle, the Cloak Bridge, the bear moat, the old town, food and how to plan a visit from Prague.
nearestAirport: Václav Havel Airport Prague (PRG), about 2.5 hours by road
knownFor: Český Krumlov Castle, the Vltava's horseshoe bend, the historic old town
budget: Kč1,800–3,500 per day, budget to mid-range

image.alt: Český Krumlov Castle above the old town

intro: Český Krumlov is genuinely one of Central Europe's most complete fairy-tale towns, its pastel old town wrapped almost entirely by a dramatic horseshoe bend in the Vltava River.
Above it all sits genuinely the country's second-largest castle complex after Prague's own, a sprawling hilltop fortress with its own bear-filled moat and a colourfully painted tower.
It's small enough genuinely to see on a day trip from Prague, though an overnight stay lets the town's cobbled lanes empty out into something genuinely magical once the tour buses leave.

whyVisit.intro: Český Krumlov's case rests genuinely on being one of the best-preserved small medieval towns anywhere in Europe.

points.title: The setting is genuinely unmatched
points.text: A near-complete horseshoe bend of the Vltava wraps the old town on three sides.

points.title: The castle is genuinely the country's second-largest
points.text: A sprawling complex with its own bear moat, painted tower and elevated Cloak Bridge.

points.title: The old town is genuinely astonishingly intact
points.text: A UNESCO World Heritage Site with barely a modern building in sight.

points.title: It's genuinely far quieter overnight
points.text: Day-trippers clear out by early evening, leaving the streets wonderfully calm.

points.title: It works genuinely well paired with Prague
points.text: An easy add-on to a Bohemia-focused itinerary, whether as a day trip or overnight stay.

attractionsIntro: Český Krumlov's essential sights are genuinely centred on its castle complex and the old town beneath it.

attractions.name: Český Krumlov Castle

image.alt: Český Krumlov Castle rising above the town

attractions.text: Genuinely the country's second-largest castle complex, its colourfully painted tower visible from almost anywhere in town.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book the interior tour ahead in summer — time slots do sell out.

attractions.name: The Cloak Bridge (Plášťový most)

image.alt: The Cloak Bridge in Český Krumlov

attractions.text: Genuinely a dramatic multi-tiered bridge connecting two parts of the castle high above the old town.
attractions.tip: Genuinely stop halfway across for one of the town's best photo viewpoints.

attractions.name: The castle's bear moat

image.file: File:Bear moat of Český Krumlov Castle.jpg
image.alt: Bears in the moat of Český Krumlov Castle

attractions.text: Genuinely a centuries-old tradition, live bears kept in the castle's moat since the 1700s.
attractions.tip: Genuinely visit late morning, when the bears tend to be most active.

attractions.name: The Castle Gardens

image.alt: The Baroque gardens at Český Krumlov Castle

attractions.text: Genuinely a peaceful baroque garden above the town, complete with a revolving summer theatre.
attractions.tip: Genuinely free to enter and a lovely, quieter escape from the busier old town streets.

attractions.name: St Vitus Church

image.file: File:Český Krumlov - At St.Vitus Church - View East.jpg
image.alt: St Vitus Church in Český Krumlov

attractions.text: Genuinely the old town's Gothic parish church, its tower offering one of the best views over the rooftops.
attractions.tip: Genuinely climb the tower if it's open — the view over the river bend is genuinely worth it.

attractions.name: The Vltava's horseshoe bend

image.alt: The Vltava River's horseshoe bend around Český Krumlov's old town

attractions.text: Genuinely the geographic feature that defines the whole town, the river wrapping the old town on three sides.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the castle tower and gardens both offer excellent views of the bend.

attractions.name: The old town's historic lanes

image.file: File:Old town in Český Krumlov with Jelení lávka, 20250504 1251 8862.jpg
image.alt: Historic lanes in Český Krumlov's old town

attractions.text: Genuinely worth simply wandering, a near-complete medieval townscape of narrow lanes and pastel facades.
attractions.tip: Genuinely explore after the day-trip buses leave for the quietest, most atmospheric version of the town.

thingsToDoIntro: Český Krumlov genuinely rewards slow wandering, split between the castle complex and the old town beneath it.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Český Krumlov Castle's interiors

image.alt: Touring the interior of Český Krumlov Castle

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential visit, taking in the castle's period-furnished rooms and elaborate masquerade hall.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely several separate tour routes cover different parts of the castle — pick one or two rather than all.

thingsToDo.title: Cross the Cloak Bridge

image.alt: The view from the Cloak Bridge in Český Krumlov

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely quick but essential stop, the bridge's elevated walkway giving one of the town's best views.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely visit close to sunset for the best light over the old town below.

thingsToDo.title: Spot the castle's resident bears

image.alt: The bear moat at Český Krumlov Castle

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely fun stop for all ages, watching the moat's bears from the bridge above.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a quick, easy stop on the way into the main castle courtyard.

thingsToDo.title: Canoe or raft the Vltava

image.alt: Canoeing on the Vltava River in Český Krumlov

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely popular warm-weather activity, paddling beneath the castle and through the old town's bend.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely rent gear from one of several outfitters right along the riverbank.

thingsToDo.title: Wander the Castle Gardens

image.alt: The Baroque Castle Gardens in Český Krumlov

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely peaceful way to spend an hour, strolling formal baroque gardens above the town.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely check for a summer performance at the garden's revolving auditorium theatre.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph the old town from a lookout

image.alt: Sunset over Český Krumlov's old town from a castle lookout

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely essential evening ritual, watching the light turn golden over the river bend and rooftops.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely the castle tower and the Cloak Bridge both make excellent sunset viewpoints.

foodIntro: Český Krumlov's food genuinely means South Bohemian classics, including a regional specialty in freshwater carp.

foods.name: Svíčková (marinated beef in cream sauce)

image.alt: Svíčková, marinated beef in cream sauce with bread dumplings

foods.text: Genuinely a reliable classic, found on nearly every traditional restaurant menu in town.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants throughout the old town.

foods.name: South Bohemian carp
foods.text: Genuinely a true regional specialty — South Bohemia's centuries-old fish ponds make carp a local staple, especially in winter.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional restaurants specialising in regional South Bohemian cuisine.

foods.name: Guláš with dumplings

image.alt: Czech goulash served with bread dumplings

foods.text: Genuinely a warming, filling option after a day of hilly castle sightseeing.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional pubs throughout the old town.

foods.name: Budweiser Budvar

image.alt: A glass of Budweiser Budvar beer

foods.text: Genuinely worth seeking out here — the original Budvar brewery sits in nearby České Budějovice, the region's capital.
foods.whereToTry: Pubs and restaurants throughout Český Krumlov.

foods.name: Smažený sýr (fried cheese)

image.file: File:Smažený sýr s tatarskou omáčkou a brambory.jpg
image.alt: Smažený sýr, breaded fried cheese with tartar sauce and potatoes

foods.text: Genuinely a satisfying pub classic, breaded fried cheese with tartar sauce and potatoes.
foods.whereToTry: Traditional pubs throughout the old town.

foods.name: Trdelník (chimney cake)

image.alt: Trdelník, a rolled pastry cooked over an open flame

foods.text: Genuinely a popular sweet treat sold from stalls throughout the old town's tourist streets.
foods.whereToTry: Street stalls throughout the old town.

bestTime.summary: Český Krumlov is genuinely at its best outside the peak summer day-tripper season.

Genuinely warm and lively, though the old town gets genuinely busy with day-trippers by midday.

Genuinely quiet and atmospheric under snow, though some attractions reduce their hours.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Český Krumlov visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely the castle interior tour online ahead in summer.
Stay genuinely overnight if you can — the town transforms once day-trippers leave.
Wear genuinely comfortable shoes — the old town and castle hill involve plenty of cobblestones and stairs.
Visit genuinely the bear moat late morning, when the bears tend to be more active.
Book genuinely a canoe or raft trip ahead in peak summer season.
Arrive genuinely early or stay late to see the old town without the day-trip crowds.

faq.q: Is Český Krumlov worth visiting from Prague?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's one of Central Europe's best-preserved medieval towns, easily reached by direct bus or train.

faq.q: Is Český Krumlov a day trip or an overnight stay?
faq.a: Genuinely either works, though an overnight stay lets you see the old town once the day-trip crowds have left, which is genuinely worth the extra time.

faq.q: How do you get from Prague to Český Krumlov?
faq.a: Genuinely easiest by direct bus, taking about 2.5 to 3 hours; a train via České Budějovice is a scenic alternative.

faq.q: Is the castle worth touring inside?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — its period-furnished rooms and masquerade hall are among South Bohemia's finest interiors.

faq.q: Are there really bears in the castle moat?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — live bears have been kept in the moat since the 18th century, a well-established local tradition.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Český Krumlov?
faq.a: One full day genuinely covers the essentials; two days allows a far more relaxed pace and an evening without the crowds.
